title: Navigation probe: gap map and task summaries
summary: High-level synthesis from a targeted navigation probe study (8 engineering and platform product participants) focused on discoverability of routes, quick-actions, and cost insights. Includes a gap map, task-level success/failure notes, and prioritized backlog with small wireframe iterations attached.
key_findings: Participants expect a single persistent quick-search (command-palette) that surfaces routes, recent models, and cost-aware suggestions — absence leads to repeated clicks and lost context.
The current left-nav groups overloaded items (models, routes, rollouts) under ambiguous labels; several users mis-clicked between 'Models' and 'Catalog' 35% of the time.
Cost signals (per-token and approximate request cost) are useful at the route level but felt intrusive at the model selection step — prefer aggregated cost badges with tooltip breakdowns.
Feature flags and rollout controls are discoverable only when users know to look in 'Release'; first-time users default to console top bar looking for 'deploy' or 'rollout'.
Users appreciated lightweight wireframe for inline route duplication (copy-with-config) — reduced manual steps in the task flow by ~40% in mock runs.
Onboarding helper microcopy is currently inconsistent (different phrasing for the same action across pages), creating doubt about irreversible actions.
Participants from platform teams wanted a keyboard-driven workflow to attach observability traces when creating a route (fast triage), which is currently a 6-click flow.
Mobile/responsive view hides important badges, causing missed cost alerts for on-call engineers using phones during incidents.
body:
Study setup: ran 90-minute remote sessions with 8 participants (mix of infra/platform engineers and ML engineers). Tasks were realistic: 1) set up a new HTTP route with a Redwood-hosted model, 2) create a canary rollout (10% traffic) with an automated fallback, 3) find the last 24h cost breakdown for a specific route, 4) duplicate an existing route and change model quantization setting, 5) attach a trace to a failing request. We used think-aloud, task timing, and success/failure markers.

Observations (detailed):
- Command pallet: 6/8 participants tried a top-right search first. When it wasn’t a universal command-palette, they resorted to left-nav search or breadcrumbs, adding 20–45s per task. Several suggested auto-complete results showing 'route: create', 'route: duplicate', and 'cost: show last 24h'.
- Left-nav nomenclature confusion: labels 'Models', 'Model catalog', 'Serving models' caused mis-routes. Suggested consolidating model-related entries under 'Models' with subitems (Catalog, Deployed).
- Rollout flows: participants expected rollout percent to be editable inline on the route list. The current flow requires drill-down to route > rollout > create causing 3 extra clicks on average.
- Cost badges: good at glance but lacked dimension (e.g., "$12.40 last 24h"). Users wanted a hover to show token count, avg latency, and bucketed cost drivers.
- Duplicate route: the proposed wireframe for 'Duplicate with edits' was tested in prototype and reduced steps. Users liked auto-incremented suffixes but wanted the original route preserved with a clear undo.
- Tracing attach: participants wanted a keyboard shortcut or context menu (right-click on request row) to attach traces. Current 'Attach' button is buried in a flyout.

Quotes captured (verbatim examples):
- "I expected to press cmd-k and type 'duplicate route' — that's muscle memory from other tools."
- "The cost number is helpful but without a token count I can't tell if it's an anomaly or expected."
- "Why are rollouts under Release? I look for 'deploy' or 'traffic' when I want to change percentages."

Metrics captured:
- Average time to create canary rollout in current console: 3m 42s. With wireframe 'inline percent edit' prototype: 2m 15s.
- Task success rate: Create route 7/8, Create canary rollout 5/8, Duplicate route (manual) 4/8, Duplicate with prototype 8/8.

Wireframe notes included in Figma: three small iterations (A/B/C) focused on: (A) command-palette prototype with fuzzy search for routes/actions, (B) condensed left-nav with clearer model taxonomy, (C) inline rollout percent control + hover cost breakdown. The A prototype was most favored by participants (preferred 6/8).
action_items: Create a lightweight RFC for global command-palette (cmd-k) that indexes routes, actions, and recent models — owner: Marco Alvarez — due: 2025-12-05
Rename left-nav items to reduce ambiguity and run A/B on label changes (Models -> Models: Catalog / Deployed) — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2025-12-15
Implement inline rollout percent control as an MVP in the route list (toggle to expand) — owner: Samir Patel — due: 2026-01-10
Add hover tooltip to cost badges showing token counts and latency percentiles — owner: Evan Brooks — due: 2026-01-20
Prototype a keyboard context menu for attaching traces from request rows and evaluate with SRE team — owner: Lina Chen — due: 2025-12-22
prioritized_backlog: P0: Global command-palette (cmd-k) + action indexing — reason: reduces average task time, high adoption in probe
P0: Inline rollout percent control in route list — reason: large win for frequent rollback/adjust workflows
P1: Cost badge tooltip with tokens & p95 latency — reason: high user value, low UI complexity
P1: Left-nav label consolidation and accessibility audit — reason: prevents mis-clicks and improves discoverability
P2: Keyboard context menu for trace attaching — reason: improves on-call efficiency, depends on infra hooks
risks_and_open_questions: Indexing sensitive artifacts in a global command-palette — need to define permission scopes and not surface private routes to lower-privilege users.
Performance impact of search indexing on large orgs — what server-side caching or pagination is required?
Analytics: what success metric do we use for command-palette adoption (unique users, average time saved, drop in clicks)?
Localization: left-nav label changes need localization review for EU/JP docs and microcopy
